piece.title: String Quartet in C major, Hob.III:32, Op.20 No.2
piece.why: Cello leads in its tenor register above Violin II and viola while Violin I is silent, then Violin I takes over, then Violin II (doubled by viola) carries the line under a Violin I pedal.

roster.label: Quartet that lost its viola: 2 violins, cello, + a clarinet

plan.summary: This is a string-quartet texture where the tune moves between parts. The cello's tenor tune in bars 0–7 goes to the clarinet so it stands out from the strings. The first violin keeps its high answer in bars 4–7 and leads the melody in bars 8–11. The viola's broken-chord and repeated-note bass goes to the real cello, which then takes the low G pedal at the close, while the clarinet joins the second violin's running eighths for the cadence.

assignments.reason: This is the opening tune (originally cello, G3–G4). The clarinet's warm low register sings it at pitch and sounds different from the strings around it.
The closing run of eighths in thirds under the second violin. It fits the clarinet's middle register, which handles this kind of fast passage easily.
The viola's broken chords and repeated Cs and Gs are the bass line here. The cello plays them at pitch and stays below everything.
The low G pedal at the cadence. The cello's open G string is ideal.
The second violin part as written, from the opening accompaniment through the harmony under the first violin to the closing eighth-note line. It all fits the player's range.
The high first-violin line: its answer to the opening phrase, the bright melody in bars 8–11 (up to D6), and the held G at the end. This needs the advanced player.
